Subject: Security exhibit — trigger matrix / pen-test window clarification

Hi David,

Thanks for routing the security exhibit draft. We are close but I want to confirm two operational details before we send this into procurement and legal:

1) Trigger matrix: when a "security incident" or a "material change" is invoked, Softera needs clarity on which items are automatically reportable vs. those that require a formal audit request. Can you confirm the list of triggers Redwood expects to consider as "audit trigger"?

2) Pen-test window: we typically coordinate a 10-business-day window for external penetration tests plus a week buffer for remediation verification. The draft MSA has a 30-day notice clause — would Redwood accept a narrower test window with the buffer described above?

Attached: SOC2 summary and our preferred pen_test_scope.xlsx for reference.

If helpful, can we hop on a 30-minute call Wednesday to align?

Best,
Emily Zhao
Security & Compliance
Softera Health

Attachments: SOC2_Report_2024.pdf (summary), pen_test_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@softera.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — trigger matrix / pen-test window clarification

Emily — thanks, and appreciate the docs. Quick answers and proposals below so legal has something concrete to review: 

- Trigger matrix: we propose a two-tier approach:
  * Tier 1 (auto-reportable): confirmed data breach involving customer PHI/PII, confirmed exfiltration, or regulatory notice within scope (e.g., HHS/FTC). Redwood would notify within 72 hours and provide incident summary.
  * Tier 2 (audit-request): significant architecture changes (e.g., new third-party storage provider), sustained degradation that might impact controls (3+ days), or customer-requested assurance beyond SOC2 scope. These would require a formal audit request from the customer and coordination with Redwood for scheduling.

- Pen-test window: we can accept a 10-business-day testing window + 5-business-day verification buffer (total 3 weeks notice cadence), but need a 14-day advance notice on scheduling from the customer to align engineering on-call and staging access.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik / Laura: can Legal accept the two-tier trigger language and the 14-day scheduling constraint? If yes, I will put this into a narrow-orderform exhibit and share for Softera legal review.

Happy to jump on Wed 3pm PT if that works.

Thanks,
David
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Note: forwarding your SOC2 to our compliance team — they may have a short follow-up.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@softera.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-23T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — trigger matrix / pen-test window clarification

Thanks David — Emily, quick legal framing from our side so procurement can move: 

- We can adopt the two-tier trigger matrix with explicit examples. We'll add a short section in the exhibit that maps each trigger to the expected Redwood response (timeline and artifacts). Example outputs for Tier 1: incident timeline, affected systems list, remediation plan, and IOCs.

- For Tier 2 audit requests: we'll include an SLA for scheduling (Redwood will propose three available windows within 14 business days of a request; final scheduling subject to mutual agreement). We will also require a standard non-disclosure attestation for any third-party auditors and limit forensic access to a scoped environment unless a broader inspection is contractually agreed.

- Pen-test window: 10 business days test + 5 business days remediation verification is acceptable. We will keep the 14-day advance notice requirement as operational standard. To avoid procurement pushback, we'll add language that Redwood will not unreasonably withhold access and will provide staging credentials and a small set of logs/artifacts for verification during the buffer period.

Action items: 
- Laura: draft the exhibit language using the bullet points above. Aim to preserve the MSA's high-level protections but give Softera the operational cadence they asked for.
- David: please upload the SOC2 summary to the shared drive and add any compliance questions the team flags.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

If you can incorporate these two tweaks, we can route the exhibit to our legal for a clean-signature Order Form.
